newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CNA expects subdued H2 shr growth.
newsitem.headline: CNA expects subdued H2 shr growth.

text.p: South African retailer CNA Gallo Ltd said on Tuesday earnings growth for the full year would remain in single digits, after a slowdown in consumer spending cut into first half profits.

Releasing CNA's interim results, which showed a modest six percent increase in headline earnings, chief executive Dennis Cuzen said: "We will maintain these numbers for the full year. It is tough out there..."
Results showed headline earnings for the six months to September 30 at 5.8 cents, up from 5.5 cents previously, hardhit by disappointing performances from two of its units, Silveray and Struik.
Cuzen said an expected hike in interest rates, which bond and stock market dealers say is inevitable given the high money market shortage, would hurt CNA's performance in the second half of the year.

However, anticipated better sales during the Christmas season, the school holiday period and preparations for the return to school in January would help the retailer achieve real growth in the next six months.
Cuzen said the viability of acquiring a 25 percent stake in confectioner Sweets from Heaven Holdings Ltd, a deal announced earlier this year, was being tested before being finally concluded.
Five test sites were being installed in selected CNA and cinema operator, Nu Metro, sites, he said.
Cuzen said a number of growth opportunities existed for Nu Metro once South Africa's gaming industry was fully operational, although this would take about another two years.
